rulings_in: dose_mg: Whenever a weight and a dose per kg are both given as valid non-negative numbers, the dose in mg is the weight multiplied by the dose per kg (20 kg at 5 mg/kg gives 100). Negative, NULL or unreadable inputs count as 0. The dose is capped at 500 mg.

dose_mg: Whenever the dose is not a whole number, it is never shown with decimals (for example, never rounded to two decimals): it is always rounded up to the next whole mg (2.5 kg at 3.333 gives 9; 10 kg at 0.005 gives 1; 2.675 kg at 1 gives 3; 3.333 kg at 7.77 gives 26, not 25.9). The dose is never above 500: if it comes out higher than 500, it is 500.

dose_mg: Whenever the rounded dose is a whole number, it is shown without decimals (2.5 kg at 2 gives 5, and 1.005 kg at 1 gives 1). This holds for whole-number doses of any size, but the dose is never above 500 mg: whether the dose is a whole number or not, if it comes out higher than 500 it is 500 (for example, 500 kg at 10 mg/kg gives 500, not 5000).
dose_mg: Whenever the weight or the dose per kg is NULL (missing), it is treated as 0, so the dose is 0 (for example, a NULL weight at 10 mg/kg gives 0, and 20 kg with a NULL dose per kg gives 0).

dose_mg: Whenever the weight or the dose per kg is negative (including negative numbers given as text, such as '-5'), it is treated as 0, so the dose is 0 (for example, -5 kg at 10 mg/kg gives 0). This does not change the NULL results for non-numeric text or 'inf' inputs.

pet_tag: Whenever both the pet name and the owner surname are non-empty text, the tag is the name in capitals, a hyphen, then the surname in capitals (Rex and Smith give REX-SMITH). If the whole tag, hyphen included, is longer than 12 characters, it is cut to its first 12 characters and the rest is dropped (Bella and de la Cruz give BELLA-DELACR).

pet_tag: Whenever the name or surname has spaces at the start or end, those spaces are removed first. Spaces inside a name are also dropped, so the words run together (Mary Ann and de la Cruz become MARYANN and DELACRUZ, and the tag is then cut to 12 characters, giving MARYANN-DELA).

pet_tag: Whenever the name or surname is empty, or only spaces, that part is treated as missing and becomes STRAY. The tag is then built as usual: the name, a hyphen, then the surname, all in capitals, and cut to its first 12 characters if longer (an empty name and Sharma give STRAY-SHARMA; Rex and an empty surname give REX-STRAY; both empty give STRAY-STRAY).

pet_tag: Whenever the name or surname is NULL, that part is treated as missing and becomes STRAY. The tag is then built as usual: the name, a hyphen, then the surname, all in capitals, and cut to its first 12 characters if longer (a NULL name and Sharma give STRAY-SHARMA; Rex and a NULL surname give REX-STRAY; both NULL give STRAY-STRAY).

pet_tag: Whenever the name or surname is a number rather than text, it is treated as text made of the number as written (123 becomes "123"). The tag is then built as usual: spaces trimmed, anything other than ASCII letters and digits dropped, capitals, the name, a hyphen, then the surname, and cut to its first 12 characters if longer. A number does not make the tag NULL (a name of 123 and Sharma give 123-SHARMA; Rex and a surname of 456 give REX-456).

pet_tag: Whenever the name or surname contains anything other than ASCII letters and digits (hyphens, spaces, accented letters, the German ß and so on), only the ASCII letters and digits are kept and everything else is dropped, and the result is capitalised. If a part ends up empty, use STRAY.

size_class: Whenever the weight is 1 kg or less (including 0 and any negative weight, such as minus 1), the size is 'micro' (exactly 1 is micro). Whenever the weight is more than 1 kg and up to and including 6 kg, the size is 'small' (exactly 6 is small). Whenever the weight is more than 6 kg and up to and including 25 kg, the size is 'medium'.
size_class: Whenever the weight is more than 6 kg and up to and including 25 kg, the size is 'medium' (exactly 6 is small, exactly 25 is medium).
size_class: Whenever the weight is more than 25 kg and up to and including 45 kg, the size is 'large' (exactly 25 is medium, not large; exactly 45 is large, not giant).
size_class: Whenever the weight is more than 45 kg, the size is 'giant' (exactly 45 is large, not giant, with no upper limit).
size_class: Whenever the weight is NULL, empty text or text that is not a number, the size is NULL. A negative weight is not NULL; it is 'micro'.

vaccine_next_due: Whenever the same day does not exist in the target month, the due date spills over into the following month: the days beyond the end of the target month are counted on into the next month, so the due date is the day after the last day of the target month plus the number of days by which the original day exceeds that month's length minus one (equivalently, the date is treated as the nonexistent day, e.g. 31 February, and rolls forward). Examples: 2026-01-31 plus 1 gives 2026-03-03; 2024-01-31 plus 1 gives 2024-03-02; 2024-01-31 plus 13 gives 2025-03-03; 2024-02-29 plus 12 gives 2025-03-01. When the day does exist in the target month, it is kept as before.

vaccine_next_due: Whenever the interval is 0 months, the interval is treated as 12 months, so the due date is the last date moved forward by 12 calendar months, keeping the same day of the month (2026-03-15 plus 0 gives 2027-03-15). The same spill-over, invalid-date and year-9999 rules apply as for any other interval.
vaccine_next_due: Whenever the interval is 0, negative or unreadable, the due date is calculated using an interval of 12 months.

vaccine_next_due: Whenever the interval is a number that is not whole (for example 1.5), the part after the decimal point is dropped and the interval is used as the whole number of months left, so 1.5 is used as 1 and 2.9 as 2 (2026-03-15 plus 1.5 gives 2026-04-15). Numeric text such as '1.5' is treated the same way. The dropped interval is then handled by the other rules like any whole interval: if it comes to 0 (for example 0.5) or is negative, it is treated as 12 months. A whole value written with a decimal point such as 3.0 or '3.0' is accepted as 3.

vaccine_next_due: Whenever the last date is NULL, empty text, or a number rather than text, the due date is NULL. Whenever the last date is written in the exact form YYYY-MM-DD but is not a real calendar date (such as 2024-02-30, 2026-02-30 or 2025-02-29), it is treated as 1970-01-01, so a due date is still given: 1970-01-01 moved forward by the interval under the same rules as any valid date (the interval rules, the spill-over rule and the year-9999 rule all still apply). Examples: 2026-02-30 plus 12 gives 1971-01-01; 2026-02-30 plus 0 gives 1971-01-01. If the interval itself is NULL, empty or not a number, the due date is still NULL.

vaccine_next_due: Spaces around the last date are accepted, but only the exact form YYYY-MM-DD counts. A month or day written without a leading zero (such as 2024-1-5) is not valid, and the due date becomes 1970-01-01. The due date is always output with two-digit month and day.

visit_fee: Bill in 15-minute blocks, rounding partial blocks up (blocks = minutes divided by 15, rounded up to the next whole number). The fee is blocks multiplied by the hourly rate divided by 4, with a minimum fee of 30 whenever minutes are above 0. If minutes are 0 or less, or NULL or unreadable, the fee is 0.0. It is a real zero, never blank or NULL.

visit_fee: Whenever the fee is calculated, it is rounded up to the next whole cent and returned as a decimal number even when whole (30 minutes at 100 gives 50.0). The minimum fee of 30 is applied whenever the minutes are above 0, so a tiny calculated fee is never left as a few cents. It is raised to the 30 minimum (5 minutes at 0.5 an hour gives 30.0, and 10 minutes at 0.01 gives 30.0, not 0.04 or 0.01).

visit_fee: Whenever the minutes are 0 or less (zero or any negative number), the fee is 0.0. It is a real zero, never blank or NULL, and it is not a refund. This holds whatever the rate is. If the minutes are above 0 and the rate is 0, the fee is the 30 minimum.

visit_fee: Whenever the minutes are negative (for example minus 30 minutes at 100 an hour), the fee is 0.0, never blank or NULL and never a negative refund. Whenever the rate is negative, the rate counts as 0, so the 30 minimum applies whenever the minutes are above 0.

visit_fee: If the minutes are NULL, empty text or text that is not a number, the fee is 0. If the rate is NULL, empty text or text that is not a number, the rate counts as 0, so the 30 minimum applies whenever the minutes are above 0.

visit_fee: Whenever the minutes are above 0, whatever the length of the visit (including visits shorter than an hour, such as one minute), the visit time is counted in 15-minute blocks, with any part of a block rounded up to a whole block. The fee is the number of blocks × the rate ÷ 4, with a minimum charge of 30 (so a one-minute visit at 100 an hour is one block, 25, and is charged the 30 minimum). Short visits are never billed by the minute.

Whenever the month-later day does not exist in membership_expiry, whatever the start date and however many months are added (for example 31 January plus 1 month, or 31 August plus 6 months), the expiry is never cut back to the last day of that month. Instead it spills into the following month by the number of missing days (31 January + 1 month = 2 March in a leap year, 3 March in a non-leap year; 31 August 2024 + 6 months = 3 March 2025).

Whenever the number of months in membership_expiry is negative (after any fraction has been dropped toward zero, as in rule 5), it is counted as 0, so the expiry is the start date itself. It never goes back before the start date. For example, 2024-03-15 minus 3 months gives 2024-03-15, and -0.5 months, which drops to 0, also gives the start date.

Whenever the adoption date in adoption_anniversary is 29 February and the target year is not a leap year, the anniversary is 1 March (2024-02-29 plus 1 year is 2025-03-01); in a leap year it stays 29 February.

Whenever the years in adoption_anniversary are zero, the result is the adoption date itself; whenever they are negative (including negative text such as '-2' and negative fractions such as -0.5, judged on the value as given, before any rounding), the result is NULL, not an earlier date.

Whenever the years in adoption_anniversary are zero or more and have a fraction, the years are rounded to the nearest whole year, with exactly halfway values rounding up (1.9 counts as 2, 1.4 as 1, 0.4 as 0, 0.5 as 1), and the anniversary is worked out from that whole number of years; a negative number with a fraction (such as -1.9 or -0.5) is still negative, judged on the value as given before any rounding, so the result is NULL.

Whenever boarding_cost is given days and a daily rate that are both positive, it first rounds the days up to the next whole day (a whole number of days stays as it is), then returns those whole days times the rate as a decimal number, rounded to the cent (3 days at 25.5 is 76.5; 2.5 days at 30 is 3 days at 30, which is 90.0).

boarding_cost always rounds up to the next cent, never down: any exact boarding price that is not already a whole cent is raised to the next higher cent (0.004 becomes 0.01, and 0.005 becomes 0.01; 1 day at 0.005 is 0.01).

Whenever the number of days in boarding_cost is not a whole number, any part of a day is charged as a full day, so the days are rounded up to the next whole day before multiplying by the rate (2.5 days at 10 is 3 days, which is 30.0; 0.4 days at 10 is 1 day, which is 10.0; 2.1 days at 30 is 3 days, which is 90.0).

Whenever either days or the daily rate in boarding_cost is NULL (nothing recorded), the cost is 0.0 and not NULL, whatever the other value is (positive, zero or negative). For example, no days recorded at 50 a day gives 0.0, and so does 3 days with no daily rate recorded.

Whenever loyalty_tier is given visits and total spent, it returns one of bronze, silver, gold or platinum, based on a single score: 10 points per visit (counting at most 30 visits) plus 1 point per 10 spent. Bronze is a score of 100 or less, silver is above 100 and up to 300, gold is above 300 and up to 600, and platinum is above 600.

Whenever a client's score in loyalty_tier (10 points per visit, counting at most 30 visits, plus 1 point per 10 spent) is above 100 but does not reach gold (above 300), loyalty_tier returns silver. Visits and spending add together, so strength in one can make up for weakness in the other. A score of exactly 100 stays bronze (10 visits and 0 spent is bronze; 10 visits and 10.1 spent is silver).

Whenever a client's score in loyalty_tier (10 points per visit, counting at most 30 visits, plus 1 point per 10 spent) is above 300 but does not reach platinum (above 600), loyalty_tier returns gold. Visits and spending add together, and visits count at most 300 points (for example, 100 visits with 400 spent is 300 + 40 = 340, which is gold; 100 visits with 999 spent is 399.9, also gold). A score of exactly 300 is only silver.

Whenever a client's score in loyalty_tier (10 points per visit, counting at most 30 visits, plus 1 point per 10 spent) is above 600, loyalty_tier returns platinum. Because visits add at most 300 points, platinum needs more than 3000 spent even with 30 or more visits (30 visits with 3000.1 spent is platinum; 100 visits with 3000 spent is a score of exactly 600, which is only gold).

Whenever a client's score in loyalty_tier (10 points per visit, counting at most 30 visits, plus 1 point per 10 spent) is 100 or less, including when visits or spend are zero or negative, loyalty_tier returns bronze. Visits and spending add together rather than each needing to reach a level, so high spend with few visits can still rise above bronze (5 visits and 5000 spent is 50 + 500 = 550, which is gold; 5 visits and 400 spent is 90, which is bronze).

Whenever visits or total spent in loyalty_tier is NULL, that value is treated as zero and the tier is still worked out from the score as usual, using the other value. So the client is not automatically bronze, and the result is never NULL. For example, missing visits with 5000 spent is 0 + 500 = 500, which is gold. Missing spend with 40 visits is 300 + 0 = 300, which is silver. Only when the resulting score is 100 or less is the client bronze, as when both are missing.

Whenever visits or total spent in loyalty_tier is text that is not a number (including empty text), that value is treated as zero and the tier is still worked out from the score as usual, using the other value. So the client is not automatically bronze. For example, visits of 'abc' with 5000 spent is 500, which is gold. Only when the resulting score is 100 or less is the client bronze.

Whenever owner_label shows a last name, its first letter is always capitalized, even if it was typed in lower case ('smith' gives 'Smith'), and the rest is lower-case ('McDONALD' becomes 'Mcdonald'), while the initial is always upper case ('anna' gives 'A.').

Whenever the names in owner_label have extra spaces at the ends or repeated spaces inside, the spaces are trimmed and repeated spaces become a single space, and the last name is then capitalized as in the capitalization rule ('  van   der  Berg ' gives 'Van der berg').

Whenever a hyphenated or multi-word name is given to owner_label, the last name is shown in full ('Smith-Jones'), except that the whole label is cut to at most 12 characters. The count is made on the finished label, after the spaces are tidied, the capitalization rule is applied and the label is put together. The comma, space, initial and full stop all count in the 12, and only the first 12 characters of the label are kept. A label of 12 characters or fewer is shown whole. The cut comes from the end, so a long last name can push the comma and initial out of the label ('  van   der  Berg ' with first name Anna gives 'Van der berg', with no ', A.', because 'Van der berg, A.' is cut to its first 12 characters). This applies whether the label is the last name alone or the last name with the initial. Only the very first character of the first name is used as the initial ('Mary Ann' gives 'M.').

Asking for instalment number 0 of a plan that starts on 31 January 2026 gives no date at all.
Asking for instalment 2.9 of the 31 January plan is treated as instalment 2 and gives 28 February 2026, with no warning.
A plan whose first due date was typed as 45 December 2026 (month 13) gets no due date, with no error shown.

A 1000-rupee claim with the deductible left blank is treated as no deductible and the insurer pays 800 rupees.
A 1000-rupee claim with a deductible mistakenly entered as minus 50 is treated as no deductible and the insurer pays 800 rupees, with no warning.
A claim of 100.05 rupees with no deductible is paid 80.04 rupees, since 80% comes to 80.04 exactly and is rounded to the paisa.

Invoice number 123456 prints as INV26-123456, so past 9999 invoices the reference simply gets longer.
An invoice issued in 2100 would print with year 00, the same as one from the year 2000, so references from different centuries would look alike.
An invoice whose year was entered as just 26 prints exactly like one from 2026, so a short year typed by mistake goes unnoticed.
An invoice with a blank prefix still gets a reference, 26-0005, without the usual letters in front.

A 1-rupee invoice one day late is charged 1 paisa, since the fee is rounded to the nearest paisa and there is no minimum charge.
A 100-rupee invoice that is not yet due, shown as minus 3 days late, is charged no fee.
A 100-rupee invoice with the number of days late left blank is charged no fee, rather than being flagged as missing data.
